hypotheses.justification: The statement does not need it to elaborate. `CohCarrier.GammaH M H := (H.comap (gamma0Units M)).map (Gamma0 M).subtype` is defined for any `M : ℕ` with no NeZero assumption (Definitions/Def_CohCarrier_Level.lean), and so are `gamma0Units` and `Gamma0_d_mul_a`. `ZMod.unitsMap hm := Units.map (castHom hm _)` needs only divisibility. The proof never uses it: it only uses `map_intCast`, `mem_GammaH_iff`, `Subgroup.mem_comap`, `Gamma0_mem` and `map_zero`, plus `simp` with `gamma0Units`, `Gamma0Map`, `ZMod.unitsMap_def` and `hcast`, and none of these needs NeZero. If simp turns castHom into ZMod.cast, `ZMod.cast_intCast` (from memory: needs `m ∣ n` and CharP, not NeZero) handles it. The statement is also true when N = 0, where ZMod 0 = ℤ: reducing mod N preserves the lower-left entry being 0 and the image of the (1,1) entry. It can be dropped on its own or together with [NeZero (N * ℓ)].

The same reasoning applies: `GammaH (N*ℓ)`, `Gamma0 (N*ℓ)` and `ZMod.unitsMap (dvd_mul_right N ℓ)` all elaborate with no NeZero instance, and no step of the proof uses one. Only the next theorem in the file uses `ZMod.unitsMap_surjective`, which requires `[NeZero m]`; this proof does not. Mathematically the identity GammaH N H' ⊓ Gamma0 (N ℓ) = GammaH (N ℓ) (comap H') holds for all N and ℓ: an element of Gamma0 (Nℓ) is in Gamma0 N by reducing mod N, and its unit image in (ZMod N)ˣ is the reduction of its image in (ZMod (Nℓ))ˣ. This is also true when Nℓ = 0. It can be dropped on its own or together with [NeZero N].
